description: How many skeleton symmetries each state has: reorderings of its atoms that keep every atom's element and implicit hydrogen count and every sigma-bonded pair (bond orders, charges and lone pairs are ignored, so resonance-equivalent atoms count as equivalent). The identity counts as one. Counts are worked out by hand in the comments. Stereo (item 12d): a symmetry must also keep every stereo mark (each mark turned to the new neighbour order); a reordering that inverts every stereocentre instead is a mirror symmetry, counted in expectedMirrorSymmetryCount where given.

cases.caseName: water with implicit hydrogens: nothing to swap
water with both hydrogens drawn: swap them
SN2 reactants: no two atoms alike
hydroxide H and alpha H differ by neighbour
carboxylate: both oxygens, despite one being drawn C=O
Br2 beside a lone bromine radical: swap the Br2 atoms
aldol alkoxide with water: swap the water hydrogens
Wittig reactants: 3! phenyl orders x 2^3 phenyl flips x 2 cyclohexanone flips
stereo: the two drawn H on a marked carbon are not swapped
stereo: trans-1,2-dibromocyclohexane keeps its two-fold rotation
stereo: in meso cis-1,2-dibromocyclohexane the swap is a mirror
stereo: an E double bond keeps the swap of its two methyl-free ends
